programs.name: PPLPPL 7 — Glute Specialization
programs.note:
Weekly layout
Day 1 — Push A + Glutes
Day 2 — Pull A
Day 3 — Legs A
Day 4 — Push B
Day 5 — Pull B
Day 6 — Legs B
Day 7 — Rest: no gym resistance training.

Home morning routines are organized for Push, Pull, and Legs gym days.

Rules
Keep all movements controlled and away from failure.
Use hand support and heel elevation as needed.
Do not force through pinching, sharp pain, or a hard joint block.
Progress by improving control, range, pauses, or reducing assistance before adding resistance.
When fatigued, perform one set of each instead of skipping everything.

entries.note: Alternate straight-back and high/kneeling variations between training blocks.
Perform during the warm-up.
Rotate with a 45° glute-biased back extension when needed. Do not perform both automatically.
Optional quad addition — perform after step-ups.

decisions.question: Approve six practical vocabulary additions for exercises the current model cannot name honestly?

decisions.question: Approve the complete 169-master classification at the existing practical level of detail?
decisions.recommended: Keep one or two ordered primary targets, meaningful secondary targets, one movement, equipment, and purpose; leave uncertain optional facts blank.

decisions.question: Approve the conservative 25-pair relationship set among the 169 source-backed masters?
decisions.recommended: Keep twenty earlier reviewed pairs and five exact-family additions. Remove the misleading standing-calf/seated-calf link, and do not convert routine choices, overlap notes, or the RDL rotation into global relationships.

decisions.question: Approve empty master notes and video IDs where the owner source supplies no stable master-level content?
decisions.recommended: Keep routine instructions scoped to entries, leave absent master notes/videos blank, use the first programmed prescription as the Library default, and keep the note-only 45° back extension default blank.

decisions.question: Approve clarifying which joint the passive internal-rotation stretch refers to?
decisions.recommended: Rename it to Gentle passive hip internal-rotation stretch and retain the earlier text as a searchable alias.

decisions.question: Approve eight external Library masters that fill four clear relationship gaps?
decisions.recommended: Add only Bodyweight squat, Goblet squat, Barbell back squat, Push-up, Barbell bench press, Dumbbell overhead press, Dumbbell lateral raise, and Dumbbell Romanian deadlift, with eight reviewed relationship edges.
